lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\OIDCIdentityProvider\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
The Composer autoloader is optimized beyond level 1. The manual allows only config.optimize-autoloader: an authoritative class map breaks the upgrade of the app, and APCu is no required extension.
vendor/ ships 1 package that the server ships itself in a major of Nextcloud 32 to 35. Both copies define the same classes, and the autoloader that is asked first decides which version runs.
9 uses of the private API of the server in 8 files. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

Nothing in the app calls 15 routes outside OCS. Looked for: a route name or a path in the PHP source and the templates, in 13 files of the frontend source and in the navigation of info.xml. A route stays behind when the frontend stops calling it. A route that only a client outside the app calls shows here as well, unless its method allows requests from other origins (CORS).

phpunit/phpunit is in require-dev of composer.json. The manual recommends a vendor-bin/ of bamarni/composer-bin-plugin per tool, so that the dependencies of a tool cannot conflict with those of the app.

lines: 1 use in 1 file of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 32 to 35. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Service/CustomClaimService.php:363 OCP\IConfig::getUserValue(): deprecated since Nextcloud 33; use IUserConfig directly

1 transaction is opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 9 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 113 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.

Nothing in the app calls 9 routes outside OCS whose method allows requests from other origins (CORS), or that answer the preflight of such a request (OPTIONS). They are there for clients outside the app, so this is no defect in itself.
